title: Specification-based Security Evaluation of Real-World Agents Tool-Calling under Long-Horizon Context Tasks
abstract: arXiv:2506.15253v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: As large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed in long-horizon unattended scenarios, security evaluation of them before deployment becomes increasingly essential and challenging. Existing evaluation methods mainly follow the paradigms of LLM-as-a-Judge or Agent-as-a-Judge. However, such judges are themselves often vulnerable to hallucination and can even be affected by perturbations. translated_title: 基于规范的真实世界智能体在长时程上下文任务中工具调用的安全评估
translated_abstract: 随着大语言模型（LLM）智能体越来越多地被部署在长时程无人值守场景中，在部署前对其进行安全评估变得愈发重要且充满挑战。现有的评估方法主要遵循LLM-as-a-Judge（以大语言模型作为评判者）或Agent-as-a-Judge（以智能体作为评判者）的范式，然而这些评判者本身往往容易受到幻觉的影响，甚至可能被扰动所干扰。此外，由于在开放式环境中逐步捕获完整环境状态的代价通常过于高昂，现有评估通常依赖于文本日志和最终的环境状态。因此，它们可能会遗漏那些在轨迹结束前被覆盖、或从未反映在文本日志中的瞬态违规行为。我们提出了RAS-Eval，一个基于规范的LLM智能体安全评估框架，该框架将效用目标与安全目标统一地表达为线性时序逻辑（LTL）规范……
tldr: 本文提出RAS-Eval框架，将效用与安全目标统一形式化为线性时序逻辑（LTL）规范，克服了现有LLM-as-a-Judge类方法易受幻觉影响、依赖文本日志和最终状态而遗漏瞬态安全违规的问题，为长时程任务中真实世界智能体的工具调用提供了更可靠的安全评估。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes RAS-Eval, a specification-based security evaluation framework that uniformly expresses utility and security objectives as Linear Temporal Logic (LTL) specifications, overcoming the hallucination susceptibility of LLM-as-a-Judge methods and their reliance on textual logs that misses transient violations, thus enabling reliable security evaluation of real-world agents' tool-calling under long-horizon tasks.
